messages:
maya: heads up — while going through the sampleapp onboarding flow I noticed personal emails in the seed data are being emitted to logs at debug level. anyone else seen this?

joel: yeah saw a stray line yesterday, thought it was a one-off. can you paste an example? :eyes:

maya: here's the exact line from local run:```2024-02-05T12:34:01.123Z INFO request_id=abc123 user.email=alice@example.com path=/signup```

sanjay: ouch. that looks like sample data made it into structured fields. is the redaction hook enabled in the sampleapp config?

clara: sampleapp currently relies on SDK autoinit for OTEL/hooks. our redact middleware lives in the express layer but autoinit instruments before express middleware runs, so logs get captured earlier.

joel: repro steps? I can try locally.

maya: yep: 1) git clone https://github.com/redwood/sampleapp 2) cp .env.example .env (LOG_LEVEL=debug) 3) npm i && npm run dev 4) hit /signup with seed payload (see samples/seed.json) 5) tail -f logs/dev.log and grep "@example.com"

sanjay: thanks. quick theory: opentelemetry SDK adds a log hook that records structured attributes before our redactor middleware runs. that order means redact never sees the logged attrs. we either need to (a) move redaction into an OTEL log processor, (b) defer autoinit when sampleapp runs, or (c) ensure sample data is scrubbed at seed generation.

telemetry-bot: Created ticket INF-523: "sampleapp: PII appears in logs during onboarding (redaction ordering)" — https://tracker.internal/INF-523 :bug:

alice: pragmatic fix suggestions: set default LOG_LEVEL=info for onboarding containers, add a quick-scrub step to the dev/start script that runs scripts/scrub-seed.sh, and add a unit test that fails if logs contain patterns like "@example.com" or email regex.

maya: I'll open a PR with the three changes — will also add a note in docs/onboarding.md about not using real addresses and how to enable dev-redaction. putting it on my plate now.

joel: awesome — assign to maya, and for follow-up, can we add a short note in SDK autoinit docs about hook ordering and a recipe to opt out?

maya: good call. I'll also add a small example showing how to register the redact processor as an OTEL log processor (so redact runs before export).

clara: for long term, research team should look at making redaction a first-class opt-in at SDK init time so onboarding/sampleapps are safe by default.

alice: thanks all. small wins: we should avoid shipping sample data that looks real — scrubbed placeholders are fine. :thumbsup:
